screen: Clients for Sufra’s app (Iqaa prototype), Sun 1 Nov 2026, 09:41. Two pages: clients.html lists every client, grouped by whose move it is. client.html?c=<key> covers one client: whose move it is now, its line with Sufra in the signature’s hand, the open order with its one action and the history evidence on the steps it bears on, every order, and the contact. The screen links back to Orders, Overview, the order page and the Ctrl/Cmd K search, which closes the loop.
decision:
MERGED, LED BY PROPOSAL A (operations first). I took four ideas from B and changed one structural choice of A.

What I checked against the code before deciding:
- Every client in sufra.js has exactly one job (13 jobs, 13 clients). No history exists, so the brief’s line “the data already exists” is only half true. Clients and current orders exist; 22 past orders and the logs of what happened have to be added as labelled demo records.
- I ran order.js’s current time spread in node. A’s claims hold:
  - Book launch reception shows as delivered Fri 30 Oct 15:00, but the event is Sat 31 Oct 18:00.
  - Office lunch’s quote link shows Sat 31 Oct 09:15. Today says 08:52.
  - SFR-26-0030 shows ‘The client approves’ as done, although Omar has not answered.
  - Every finished order shows ‘Wait two days’ and ‘Remind the client’ as done.
  - Every delivery lands about a day before its event.
  - en-GB toLocaleString prints ‘Mon 7 Sept’.
  - In Africa/Cairo (the user’s zone), local parsing makes Huda’s 29 Oct 13:15 → 30 Oct 10:00 answer last 21.75 h instead of 20.75 h, because of Egypt’s DST change.
  - So a shared clock with UTC parsing must ship with this screen. Otherwise the client page and the order page contradict each other.
- I ran A’s 22 past orders through a checker. All pass:
  - every due and finished label matches its weekday;
  - events are in order;
  - a reminder exists exactly when no answer came within 48 h;
  - codes 0001–0022 were all opened before 0023;
  - every arrival is within an hour of its event;
  - lateness is computed, not stored: 0013 was 15 min late and 0018 was 20 min late.
- Contrast (tools/color.py): red 4.93, violet 4.94, n700 8.16, n600 5.65, n500 3.95, n400 2.85. Build’s dashed outline uses n400, which is below 3:1, so these pages use n500.
- Measured in the running preview at 1440×900:
  - the sheet content is 1110 px (32 px gutters plus a 10 px scrollbar);
  - order.html’s grid is main 682 + side 380;
  - its journey band is 215 px tall, because the stretched SVG is 878×165;
  - at 375, 4 tabs of 64×54 fit.

Why A leads:
- The brief says Clients closes the loop with Orders. A’s list answers the question a list is opened for (whose move it is: clients to chase, clients to serve, clients with nothing open). It uses the same glyph vocabulary as Orders’ ‘who’ column, so both screens read the same.
- A’s best idea is the one that makes history useful. History appears as evidence on the exact step it predicts: under ‘Omar approves’, “Omar answered both earlier quotes only after Iqaa’s reminder.” This leads to one person-made action (Remind Omar now), and that action passes the identity’s own test: the decision is violet, the act is ink.
- A’s data fix is more truthful than B’s station count. SFR-26-0030 moves from step 1 to step 0, because the quote went out at 08:52 and the job waits on Omar, not on a timer. Overview (1→2), the Orders map (2) and the order page then agree, with no filter change.

Changed from A: ‘Line with Sufra’ moves directly under the head, as order.html’s journey band already does.
- With A’s order the band would start around y≈900 at 1440×900, below the fold. The user’s explicit request would be hidden.
- With the band first (about 144 px tall at a fixed k 1.25) and the action row placed right under the open order’s header, the action still sits at y≈470–520.

Taken from B:
- The rounds data model. It covers changes and per-round reminders.
- A change is drawn as a second arch, not A’s straight followed by an arch. One stroke must mean one thing in the legend.
- A first order shows one dashed word after Now: the line starts here.
- A red ‘15 min late’ label sits over a late word only.
- One grammar rule is added to signature.html so the client word is documented, not invented.
- Computed copy never uses pronouns for a client.

Rejected from B, with reasons in ‘rejected’: the month clock on the list, tabs with ‘Quiet’ and two invented clients, the habits KPI strip, the notes form, and the reminder as a Watar draft. Watar stays for Ask Watar, the next screen.

Expected side effects, all intended and re-captured:
- Overview ‘Waiting on clients’ goes from 1 to 2.
- The Orders row for 0030 reads ‘Waiting for Omar’.
- Every order page gets real times.
- Hala’s Today ‘Coming to you’ swaps 0030 and 0033 (k 2 vs 3).
- The orders/overview captures change, and screens.html gains an eighth screen.

sections.name: Between Sufra and <C>: steps and evidence (client.html)
sections.content: h3 ‘Between Sufra and Omar’ with the hint ‘Only the steps that reach Omar’. Rows are the steps that reach the client (receipt, quote link, approval, wait, remind, arrival time, delivery, invoice). They run from the last one done (or the first, if none) through ‘Yusuf delivers’, or to the end once the job is past delivery. ‘Wait two days’ and ‘Remind the client’ appear only while the job sits on the approval step or after they ran; skipped steps never appear. In step names ‘the client’ becomes C: ‘Omar approves’, ‘Remind Omar’, ‘Send Omar a receipt’. Darb’s 6 rows: Send the quote link · done · ‘08:52’ | Omar approves · now · ‘Waiting, 49 min’ — evidence ‘Omar answered both earlier quotes only after Iqaa’s reminder.’ | Wait two days · dashed · ‘Until Tue 3 Nov, 08:52’ | Remind Omar · dashed · ‘Tue 3 Nov, 08:52’ — ink bold ‘That is after the office lunch on Mon 2 Nov, 12:30.’ | Send the arrival time · dashed · ‘Ahead’ | Yusuf delivers · dashed · ‘Mon 2 Nov, by 12:30’ — ‘Both earlier deliveries arrived on time (12:10, 12:15).’ Other evidence, computed. Nakhla, on ‘Maha approves’: ‘Maha answered both earlier quotes within 2 hours.’ Wadi, on ‘Rami approves’: ‘Rami’s earlier answers took 4 hours 25 min (one change) and 40 min. For the board breakfast on Tue 6 Oct, Rami asked for a change: “No dairy for two guests”.’ Iqaa makes no claim about the menu; Reem connects it with the labneh in the draft. Hayat, on ‘Rania approves’: ‘Rania’s earlier answers took 2 days 9 hours (after the reminder) and 3 days 6 hours (one change). For the volunteer lunch on Sat 26 Sep, Rania asked for a change: “A vegetarian main for 10 guests”.’ Majal, on ‘Yusuf delivers’ (now, ‘By 16:00 today’): ‘Late once before: Sun 4 Oct, 16:15 for 16:00.’ (only ‘Late’ red). A finished approval shows ‘Answered in 20 hours 45 min’ (Huda). A first order shows ‘First order: nothing to compare yet.’

Approve it or ask for a change: sufra.iqaa.app/q/0030’. sections.content: tools/p_screens.py gains an eighth entry after Orders. id ‘clients’, name ‘Know every client’, url ‘sufra.iqaa.app/clients’, open ‘Open Clients’, what: ‘The owner sees whose move it is with every client, and opens one to see its open order, its line with Sufra and every order before.’ ids: (1) ‘Each client’s history is written in the signature’s hand: an arch for every answer Sufra waited for, a lifted pen and a straight where Iqaa had to remind them, a red snap where Sufra arrived late.’ (2) ‘History is evidence at the step it predicts: under “Omar approves”, that Omar answered both earlier quotes only after the reminder.’ (3) ‘The decision is violet, the act is ink: reminding Omar early is a person’s button, and the pen writes the reminder into his line.’ The head text changes ‘Seven screens’ to ‘Eight screens’. signature.html (p_mark.py ENCODE) gains one rule (see identity_details).

identity_details: Whose move is drawn, not put in a pill. The step’s own glyph leads the list column and the state box: the violet arch when the quote is with the client, the team member’s lilac initial (.av) when Sufra’s people hold it, the ink straight when it runs by itself. This is the same vocabulary as Orders’ .or-who, so a glance reads the same on both screens.
One stroke, one meaning. A straight in a client’s line always means ‘Iqaa reminded them’. Proposal A’s straight before a second arch would also have meant ‘a new quote went out’, so it was dropped.

The decision is violet, the act is ink. ‘Remind Omar now’ is a violet button only when the line’s own reminder (quote + 48 h) would come later than a day before the event. Today that is only Darb Studio: due Tue 3 Nov, 08:52, after the lunch on Mon 2 Nov, 12:30. What Iqaa then does is an ink straight, which the pen writes in a quarter beat (150 ms, ease-move). It is the only motion on either page, and it has a cause.

Red never predicts. A coming risk is stated in ink bold words. Red marks only deliveries recorded late, always with the snap and the word ‘late’: Majal Hub on Sun 4 Oct (16:15 for 16:00) and Bina Studio on Mon 12 Oct (12:50 for 12:30).

No client logos, avatars or invented marks. Lilac circles stay reserved for Sufra’s people. Organization marks belong to organizations on Iqaa.
The brand lives in 18–24 px glyphs, the small mini lines and one band. No hero mark.
The sidebar count on Clients (2, the clients whose answer the line waits for) is set in n600, not violet. Violet stays for what waits for you.

Documented, not improvised. p_mark.py ENCODE gains this rule: ‘A client’s history is written order by order with the steps that reached the client: an arch for each answer the line waited for, a lifted pen and a straight where the wait ran out and Iqaa reminded them, then the delivery — a loop, or the snapped red stroke when it arrived late. The pen lifts between orders, because each is its own job.’

Watar stays in its lane here. Its quote drafts are shown with the waiting arch, as on Today (‘Watar’s draft, waiting for Reem’). Suggesting actions is left to Ask Watar, the next screen, where its drafts will use the dashed grey pen.
computations: Demo time and parsing (jobs.js views). S.now = '2026-11-01T09:41'. Every demo ISO string is parsed as UTC: U(iso) = new Date(iso + 'Z'), read with getUTC*. Labels come from fixed arrays DAY = ['Sun', …, 'Sat'] and MON = ['Jan', …, 'Dec']: label = 'Tue 1 Sep, 08:30', and a time on 1 Nov prints as '08:52' alone. Never use toLocaleString: en-GB prints 'Sept'. Never parse local time: in Africa/Cairo, 29 Oct 13:15 → 30 Oct 10:00 measures 21.75 h instead of 20.75 h across Egypt’s DST change. The live clock on client.html is 09:41 plus whole minutes since load, refreshed every 60 s, as Today does.

Client key and short name. j.ck is computed in sufra.js (see data_additions). The short name C is the contact, or the name for a private client. A name starting ‘Dr ’ stays whole; otherwise C is the first word: Omar, Rania, Dr Nadia, Lina, Huda, Sami, Samer, Aseel. No pronoun is ever used for a client: the copy repeats C.

A client’s orders = S.jobs.concat(S.past) filtered by ck. open = not finished, sorted by iso ascending. finished = finished, sorted by iso ascending. facts(order): rounds = log.rounds || []; answered = the last round has an answer; took = last.answer − rounds[0].sent; reminded = any round has reminded; changes = the rounds that carry a change; arrived = log.arrived; late = minutes of (arrived − iso) when above 0, so 0013 is 15 and 0018 is 20.

Durations in words. Under 60 min: 'N min'. Under a day: 'H hour(s)[ M min]'. A day or more: 'D day(s)[ H hour(s)]', with hours rounded to the nearest hour. Examples: Darb’s answers took 2 days 5 hours and 2 days 22 hours; Hayat’s SFR-26-0010 took 3 days 6 hours; Huda’s took 20 hours 45 min; at 09:41 Omar has been waiting 49 min and Rania 22 hours 11 min.

Group, sort and summary. side = 'none' if there is no open order; 'theirs' if J.stepOf(soonest open).who === 'The client'; otherwise 'ours'. Theirs sorts by iso. Ours sorts by iso, with jobs past the Deliver station placed last (Overview’s delivered(): idx(at) > idx('deliver')). None sorts by its last finished order’s iso, newest first. Summary: `${clients} clients · ${open jobs} with an order on the line · ${theirs} waiting on their answer` = ‘13 clients · 10 with an order on the line · 2 waiting on their answer’.

Reminder and risk, for an open round. The rest step’s who is read from the Client approval station through REST_H = { 'Two days': 48, 'A day': 24 } hours; the line definition is not changed. due = open round.sent + REST_H. risk = due > event − 24 h, because the line reminds the kitchen a day before. after = due > event. Darb: due Tue 3 Nov, 08:52; risk and after. Hayat: due Mon 2 Nov, 11:30; no risk. The violet primary button shows only when risk is true.

History phrase, from finished orders F. If F is empty: ‘First order’. Otherwise collect the parts, in this order: late (‘Late once, Sun 4 Oct’, or ‘Late N times’); reminded (‘Reminded r of n’); changes (‘N change(s)’). If there are no parts: ‘One order, on time’ when n = 1, else ‘On time, n of n’. Parts are joined with ‘ · ’, and every fact is kept (no first-match-wins).

Answer sentence. E = ‘earlier ’ when the client has an open order, else ''. quotes = ‘the E quote’, ‘both E quotes’ or ‘all n E quotes’. (a) Every order reminded: ‘C answered {quotes} only after Iqaa’s reminder’. The band adds ‘: after d1, then d2’ (three or more: ‘d1, d2 and d3’). (b) No reminder and no change: for n = 1, ‘C answered the E quote in d’. Otherwise the band reads ‘C answered {quotes} in min to max’, and the step evidence reads ‘C answered {quotes} within ⌈max⌉ hours’ (‘an hour’ when it is 1). (c) Mixed, n ≤ 3: ‘C’s E answers took d (after the reminder|one change) and d …’, newest first. (d) Mixed, n > 3: ‘C answered in min to max; Iqaa reminded C r of n times.’ Change sentence, evidence only, from the newest finished order with a change: ‘For the {title, lower-cased first letter} on {Day d Mon}, C asked for a change: “{text}”.’ Delivery sentence, when any order was late: ‘Late once{ before}: Sun 4 Oct, 16:15 for 16:00.’ (‘ before’ is added in step evidence). Otherwise: ‘{The E delivery|Both E deliveries|All n E deliveries} arrived on time’, plus ‘ (12:10, 12:15)’ when n ≤ 3 and every event had the same time. Band reading = answer + delivery sentences. Approval-row evidence = short answer + change sentence. Delivery-row evidence = delivery sentence with ‘before’. A finished approval row shows ‘Answered in {took}’. With no history: ‘First order: nothing to compare yet.’

Word strokes for one order. For each round: an arch ('held'), with state done if the round has an answer, now if the round is open and the job sits on the approval step. If that round was reminded, add 'rest' then 'run' (done). If there are no rounds yet: one 'held' (next). Then the delivery: 'failed' when late, otherwise 'struck'; done if arrived, now if the job sits on ‘Yusuf delivers’, otherwise next. A reminder sent from this page appends a 'run' (done) after the open arch. Strokes are drawn with IQ.cell(kind, x, 0, IQAA.pal.light, k, state === 'next'): the dashed pen is #807E91 with dasharray 1.4 × pen.

Band geometry. Each stroke is 24 units (IQ.WIDTH); words are separated by a 12-unit pen lift. k = 1.25 when the band is at least 640 px wide, else 1. Widths at k 1.25: Darb 330 px, Hayat 300, Majal 360, Al-Shifa 360, Bina 285, Wadi 240, Nakhla 210, Sami Khoury, Huda and Dar Qalam 135, Aseel, Lina and Samer 60. At k 1: Darb 264, Majal and Al-Shifa 288. The Now tick x = max(the middle of the client-facing stroke the job is on, the end of the last solid stroke) + 6 units. A date label sits under each word; ‘N min late’ sits over a late word. Fit rule: if the width at k is larger than the cell, lower k toward 0.8; still too wide, then show the newest words that fit and add ‘+N earlier’ (a link to #orders).

Mini line in the list: finished words only, at k 0.6, with 7.2 px lifts. Widths: Darb 122.4, Hayat 108, Majal 136.8, Bina 136.8, Wadi 79.2, Nakhla 64.8, singles 28.8, Al-Shifa 172.8. The history column is 237 px at 1440 and 199 px at 1280 (sidebar open), and at least 187 px wherever the 4-column row applies (900 px container and up), so every line fits. Each mini line is an SVG about 27 px tall, aria-hidden.

Whose move lines. Theirs: line 1 is the arch with ‘Waiting for C since {at(open round.sent)}’. Line 2 is ‘Reminder due {due}, after the {title, lower-cased first letter}’ (ink bold) when the reminder lands after the event, ‘…, less than a day before the {title}’ when it is risky but before, or ‘Reminder due {due} if there’s no answer’. Ours: line 1 is the .av initial with ‘{who} · {doing}’ for a person, or the step glyph with ‘Runs by itself · {doing}’ (‘Waits · …’ for a rest). Line 2, first match: past Deliver → ‘Delivered {at(arrived)}’; S.done sent the arrival time → ‘C has had the arrival time since {time}’; the quote was answered → ‘C approved the quote {at(answer)}’; no round yet → ‘The quote hasn’t gone to C yet’. DOING table in jobs.js, keyed by step name: Reem logs the order → logging the order · Send the client a receipt → sending {C} a receipt · Watar drafts the quote → checking Watar’s draft of the quote · Reem checks the prices → checking the prices · Send the quote link → sending {C} the quote · Wait two days → waiting two days for {C}’s answer · Remind the client → reminding {C} · Create the shopping list → writing the shopping list · Buy the materials → buying the materials · Hala orders from the wholesaler → ordering from the wholesaler · Wait for the delivery → waiting for the wholesaler’s delivery · Remind the kitchen a day before → reminding the kitchen · Salma prepares → preparing the {title, lower-cased} · Send the arrival time → sending {C} the arrival time · Yusuf delivers → delivering by {HH:MM} {V.when} · Create the invoice → writing the invoice · Send the invoice → sending the invoice.

State box. Nothing open: the loop glyph and ‘Nothing open · last order finished {finished}’. Theirs: the arch and ‘Waiting on C’s answer to the quote for the {title, lower-cased} {today|tomorrow|on Day d Mon}’. A person: the .av and ‘With {who}: {doing}’. Runs: the glyph and ‘Runs by itself: {doing}’. With 2+ open orders: ‘ and N more open’.

Steps between Sufra and C. REACH (a Set in jobs.js, keyed by step name) = Send the client a receipt, Send the quote link, The client approves, Wait two days, Remind the client, Send the arrival time, Yusuf delivers, Send the invoice. Rows are the REACH steps of the job’s route from the last done one (or the first) through ‘Yusuf delivers’, or to the end once the job is past Deliver. Skip states are excluded. Wait and Remind are excluded unless the job sits on the approval step or they are done. Times: done uses V.clock. The now approval row reads ‘Waiting, {live duration}’; now Yusuf delivers reads ‘By {HH:MM} {when}’. Next rows: Wait reads ‘Until {due}’, Remind reads ‘{due}’ (both only while a round is open), Yusuf delivers reads ‘{Day d Mon}, by {HH:MM}’, anything else reads ‘Ahead’.

Shared clock V.clock(j), in jobs.js views, replacing order.js’s even spread. (1) The steps are the job’s route, with state done, now or next as today. (2) Skip: ‘Wait two days’ and ‘Remind the client’ get state 'skip' when the job is past them, its last round is answered, and no round was reminded. (3) Fixed points: step 0 at opened (the order is logged as it comes in) · ‘Send the quote link’ at rounds[0].sent · ‘The client approves’ at the last answer · ‘Wait two days’ and ‘Remind the client’ at reminded · ‘Yusuf delivers’ at arrived · each S.done entry gives its step at today’s time, and the run steps listed after it in d.kinds take the same minute · a finished job’s last step at its finished label. (4) A run step right after a fixed step takes the latest fixed time so far (through skipped steps), unless it is fixed itself. (5) Every other done step is spread over 08:00–18:00 UTC working hours between the latest earlier fixed time and the next fixed time (the end is S.now for open jobs), rounded to the quarter hour and clamped inside. Checked in node with identical results under TZ=UTC and TZ=Africa/Cairo. 0030: logs the order and sends the receipt Wed 28 Oct, 13:15; Watar drafts Fri 30 Oct, 11:00; prices and quote link Sun 1 Nov, 08:52; now The client approves. 0027: Wait and Remind are skipped; Salma prepares and Send the arrival time at 09:05. 0014: quote link Wed 30 Sep, 11:10; wait and remind Fri 2 Oct, 11:10; approves Sat 3 Oct, 09:25; shopping list Sat 3 Oct, 09:25; delivers Mon 5 Oct, 12:15; invoice sent Tue 6 Oct, 10:20.

Orders list cells on the client page. Their answer: no round yet → ‘Quote not sent yet’; an open round → ‘Waiting since {at(sent)}’; otherwise ‘{took}’, plus ‘, after the reminder’ if reminded, plus ‘, after a change: “{text}”’ if changed. Delivery: arrived → ‘{HH:MM} · on time’ or ‘{HH:MM} · N min late’ (with the snap glyph, the late part in red); not yet → ‘Ahead’.

Search, on the list and in the palette: the query is lower-cased and matched as a substring against `${name} ${contact} ${codes and titles of all its orders}`. ‘Found in {code}, {title}’ shows when the name and the contact do not match. The live region reads `${n} ${n === 1 ? 'client matches' : 'clients match'}`.

Contact card. The phone label is ‘WhatsApp’ when by is 'WhatsApp', otherwise ‘Phone’. Channel hint: ‘Quotes, reminders and arrival times go to C by {WhatsApp|email}.’ Their link is sufra.iqaa.app/q/{last 4 digits of the soonest open code}. First order = the earliest opened order: ‘First order: {code}, {title}, {Day d Mon of its event}’.

Reminder message preview: ‘Hi C, a reminder: Sufra’s quote for your {title, lower-cased} {today|tomorrow|on Day d Mon} at {HH:MM} is waiting for your answer. Approve it or ask for a change: sufra.iqaa.app/q/{code4}’.

Long history (beyond this data): in the band, k is lowered to 0.8 at most, then the newest words with ‘+N earlier’ linking to #orders. In list rows, the newest words that fit, led by ‘+N’.

Unknown key: client.html?c=xyz shows ‘No client called “xyz”.’ and ‘It may have been typed wrong. See every client.’ (a link). This mirrors order.js’s not-found state; the band, grid and orders are hidden.

accessibility: Each list row is one link, with no nested interactive element. Its aria-label starts with the visible name, so the label contains the name (WCAG 2.5.3), and reads the row as a sentence. Example: ‘Darb Studio, Omar. Office lunch for 18 people, Mon 2 Nov at 12:30, tomorrow. Waiting for Omar’s answer since 08:52; the line’s reminder, Tue 3 Nov at 08:52, would come after the office lunch. History: reminded 2 of 2.’

Mini lines are aria-hidden; the phrase carries their meaning. The band SVG has role=img and a sentence label, e.g. ‘Darb Studio’s orders with Sufra. Mon 7 Sep: Sufra waited for Omar’s answer, two days passed, Iqaa reminded Omar, delivered on time. Mon 5 Oct: the same. Mon 2 Nov: waiting for Omar’s answer now; the delivery is ahead.’ The legend is a real ul.

Every state is told by shape and by words, never by colour alone. Late has the snap, the word ‘late’ and red. Waiting has the arch and ‘Waiting for’. Ahead has the dashed pen and ‘Ahead’. A risk is ink bold words, not red.

Structure. One h1 per page; h2 for the groups and the page sections (Line with Sufra, Open now, Orders, Contact); h3 for ‘Between Sufra and C’. Groups, rows, steps and orders are ol. The contact and each order’s cells are dl. Times use <time datetime='2026-11-01T08:52'>; codes use <code>.

Targets. List rows are at least 72 px; buttons and the search are 44 px; tabs are 52 px or more (measured 64×54 at 375). ‘Show every client’ uses .btn (44 px), not .btn.small (36 px). Focus is the frame’s 2 px violet outline at offset 2 everywhere, including row links.

Reminder confirm. When it opens, focus moves to ‘Send the reminder’. Esc or Cancel closes it and returns focus to ‘Remind Omar now’. After sending, focus moves to the status line (role=status, tabindex -1), which is announced.

DOM order equals reading order at every width: head, band, Open now, Contact, Orders. On desktop, grid areas only place Contact in the side column. No CSS order changes the sequence (the existing .row-act primary-first rule on phones is kept as on other screens).
The search has an sr-only label and a polite live region that announces the match count. The sidebar count reads ‘2 waiting on their answer’.
Bracketed placeholders such as [PHONE] and [ADDRESS] carry sr text ‘not added yet’. The phone and email are plain text, not dead tel: or mailto: links.
Reduced motion: the only animation, the reminder stroke, is replaced by its final state. Hover styles apply only with (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine).

RTL readiness: logical properties only (padding-inline, inset-inline-start, border-block). SVGs carry direction: ltr until the Arabic phase writes signatures right to left, as decisions.html requires.
Computed copy never guesses gender: it repeats the client’s short name instead of a pronoun.
